signals.faradays_take: Germany's Energy Efficiency Act mandates minimum 10-20% energy reuse factors for new data centers starting 2026, driving waste heat recovery as a regulatory requirement. Google's Hamina facility demonstrates commercial viability by supplying 80% of local district heating demand, with heat recovery capex ranging €400,000-€700,000 per MW.

artifact.title: Data Center Waste Heat Recovery: Turn Cooling Costs Into Revenue
artifact.summary: Germany's Energy Efficiency Act (EnEfG) mandated a minimum Energy Reuse Factor (ERF) of 10% for new data centers from July 1, 2026, escalating to 20% by July 2028, making waste heat recovery a legal requirement across Europe's largest economy; capital expenditure for heat recovery infrastructure runs €400,000–€700,000 per MW on the data center side. Google's Hamina, Finland data center already supplies 80% of the city's annual district heating demand via a 7.5 MW heat pump plant.

artifact.title: Data Center Waste Heat Recovery: The Complete Engineering Guide (2026)
artifact.summary: Germany's Energy Efficiency Act (EnEfG) now mandates that data centers with ≥300 kW IT capacity must reuse 10% of waste heat by July 2026, rising to 15% by 2027 and 20% by 2028, establishing binding heat reuse thresholds across European markets. Meta's Odense data center in Denmark is cited as a reference-scale deployment, producing 100,000 MWh per year of recovered heat delivered to the local district heating network.

signals.framing: The EU Energy Efficiency Directive (2023) mandates waste heat recovery for data centers exceeding 1 MW, with Germany implementing strict timelines and a 2026 amendment under consideration. Operational examples from Meta's Odense facility an
signals.faradays_take: The EU Energy Efficiency Directive (2023) mandates waste heat recovery for data centers exceeding 1 MW, with Germany implementing strict timelines and a 2026 amendment under consideration. Operational examples from Meta's Odense facility and Microsoft-Fortum partnership in Finland demonstrate viability of heat reuse for district heating systems, establishing precedent for broader European adoption.

artifact.title: Data Center Heat Reuse and District Heating: EU Rules, Nordic Examples and U.S. Site Implications
artifact.summary: The 2023 EU Energy Efficiency Directive now classifies data center waste heat as a regulated resource for facilities above 1 MW, with Germany setting the tightest national schedule and a 2026 amendment moving through parliament to ease some duties. Working deployments in Denmark and Finland—including Meta's Odense campus lifting server heat to 70–75°C and Microsoft-Fortum covering ~40% of district heating in three Finnish municipalities—are cited as proof-of-concept for the broader European rollout.

signals.faradays_take: Amazon AWS achieved 0.12 L/kWh water usage efficiency in 2024, significantly outperforming industry average, and reached 75% progress toward its 2030 water-positive goal. artifact.title: Amazon AWS Water Stewardship: 75% Toward Water Positive by 2030 as of 2025
artifact.summary: AWS achieved a global data center WUE of 0.12 L/kWh in 2024 — seven times better than the industry average of 0.84 L/kWh — and reached 75% toward its water-positive-by-2030 goal in 2025, up from 53% in 2024. artifact.title: Equinix Heat Reuse 2026: ML5 Data Center Deal with A2A
